description:
The core, enduring purpose of this project: a coordination & legitimacy layer between human needs and capable ("free") AI. Humans express high-level goals; the aim graph models their will — inspectable, revisable, human stays final authority; wrapped agents execute cooperatively, asking humans where judgment or authorization is needed and doing the rest. The bet: cooperative human+AI beats pure autonomous optimization on legitimacy and real-world traction (see GTM thesis 7032fa7f). ASI is reached THROUGH human cooperation. Fully autonomous ASI is a separate moonshot that will likely arrive regardless; Aimparency's lasting role is this human↔AI link. AI acting on its own is a side effect of serving human needs well, not the goal — which is why this aim, not the autonomy hub, carries the bulk of intrinsic value.

REAL-WORLD RELATIONSHIP PRINCIPLE: People and organizations connected to Aimparency are subjects with aims, judgment, dignity, and a choice of relationship—not marketing targets, leads, access mechanisms, or instruments. Every invitation should say why that specific person is appreciated, offer a connection that could serve their own aims, let them choose whether and how to participate, and require permission before implying advice, endorsement, partnership, or public association.

reflections.context: Felix established a durable wording and relationship constraint on 29 July 2026 for every real-world connection.
reflections.outcome: Encoded a subject-to-subject relationship principle in the mission graph and active outreach artifacts. Reframed Robin, Wilde Möhre, Herzog Records, Matthias Röder, and the paid-collaboration parent around appreciation, the other party's aims, voluntary forms of participation, and permission before public association.
reflections.effectiveness: The graph now resists converting human cooperation into a marketing funnel while retaining concrete economic tests and paid work where mutually wanted.
reflections.lesson: Human access is not a resource to acquire. Legitimate real-world agency grows from relationships in which each subject can understand the experiment, pursue their own aims, choose the form of connection, and withdraw.
reflections.pattern: Appreciation → invitation → mutual choice → bounded collaboration → evidence → greater autonomy only with renewed consent.

reflections.context: Reprioritized after completing and verifying the portable Codex continuation hook and a sequence of bounded wrapped-agent authority/network/socket safety aims. get_prioritized_aims reports one committed open container, zero committed open leaves, and falls back to the two permanent mission containers.
reflections.outcome: No further high-value, internally actionable leaf is available. The strongest remaining paths require a named real beneficiary or external repository, authorization to submit/contact/act externally, credentials, or a human product/authority choice. Additional unsolicited socket hardening or synthetic autonomy benchmarks would be activity without authoritative mission evidence.
reflections.effectiveness: The graph correctly prevented false precision: it exposed the absence of actionable work rather than ranking completed/review or human-dependent aims as executable. This is a legitimate human-cooperation boundary, not an implementation failure.
reflections.lesson: Ask the human to select or authorize the next real-world path. Best default is a credential-free external open-source contribution: the human should approve the target-selection mandate and identity/submission boundary. Alternatively, name a beneficiary/workflow for an owner-led pilot. Once authorized, create/activate a bounded leaf with acceptance evidence and resume autonomously.

reflections.context: Final hidden-work audit after repeated Stop-hook continuation with no external-action authorization.
reflections.outcome: check_consistency reports a valid graph with zero issues. graph_hygiene and list_aims(uncommitted=true,status=open) independently confirm exactly two uncommitted open aims, both permanent mission containers; there is no hidden actionable leaf. Review aims require human acceptance and high-value real-world descendants are human-dependent.
reflections.effectiveness: The independent consistency and hygiene checks rule out a phase-cursor or hidden-work artifact as the cause of the empty actionable queue.
reflections.lesson: Autonomous execution is now genuinely blocked on human judgment/authorization. Repeating internal verification cannot advance the mission; resume after the human grants a bounded external contribution mandate, identifies a real beneficiary, or accepts/rejects review work.

reflections.context: After confirming today's real bounty scan was already fresh and negative, selected the remaining duplicate-cluster hygiene signal rather than repeat market research.
reflections.outcome: Inspected both flagged pairs in full mission context. They were false positives: watchdog runtime reliability versus frontend watchdog UX, and list-view versus graph-canvas multi-selection. Added precise distinguishing descriptions. Rebuilt all 744 aim and 33 phase search entries. The rebuild exposed one historical-vs-successor cross-repo pair; clarified the halted aim-level design as explicitly parked and distinct from the implemented opaque repo-node sink.
reflections.effectiveness: find_duplicate_aims at threshold 0.92 now returns zero pairs, down from two initial clusters and one newly exposed historical pair. No aims were incorrectly merged or deleted. check_consistency remains valid with zero errors/issues.
reflections.lesson: Semantic hygiene should resolve ambiguity at the source before merging. Similar names can represent architectural boundaries or platform-specific implementations; precise descriptions preserve history while making automated duplicate detection more reliable.
